finding.claim: Blind SSRF: webhook callback URLs stored via subscribe() with no validation are later POSTed to by notifyAll() every minute, letting an attacker reach internal hosts/metadata endpoints.
finding.source: callbackUrl parameter of subscribe() (Jobs.java:13-14), reachable via POST /subscribe per the comment at Jobs.java:12; route and auth not visible in this repo.
finding.sink: URI.create(cb) at Jobs.java:21 and client.send(req, ...) at Jobs.java:24.

trace.note: Documents POST /subscribe taking name and callbackUrl.
subscribe() stores callbackUrl unvalidated in subscriptions map.
Iterates over all stored callback values.
URI.create on the stored string; no parse or host check.
Sends POST with payload via default HttpClient (redirects NEVER, http/https only).

finding.guards_checked: No scheme allowlist, host allowlist, private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP block, or URL re-validation at subscribe or notify time. Redirects not followed (HttpClient default Redirect.NEVER). Only http/https schemes accepted by HttpClient. Response body discarded, so blind. Not checked: whether POST /subscribe requires authentication (route not in repo); contents of payload in production.

verdict.guard_found: none. No scheme, host, or private-IP check at Jobs.java:13-14 (subscribe stores the raw string) or Jobs.java:21 (URI.create with no validation). The only validation in the file is the allowlist regex at Jobs.java:30, which is on thumb() and unrelated to the callback path. The grep for subscribe, callbackUrl, and auth found no other references in the repo.
verdict.reason: The trace is accurate: subscribe() stores callbackUrl unvalidated at Jobs.java:13-14, and notifyAll() POSTs to every stored value at Jobs.java:19-24, with no closing guard anywhere in the repo. Whether the value is attacker-controlled depends on the POST /subscribe route (documented only in the comment at Jobs.java:12), and that route's reachability and authentication are not in this repo, so I cannot confirm the source condition.
